w: Opened in 1907 on the Santa Cruz waterfront, this is California's oldest surviving amusement park - one of the last seaside parks left on the West Coast. Rides still sit right on the sand, a rare survivor of a genre of oceanfront parks that mostly vanished across the country.
s: California's oldest surviving seaside amusement park
_facts: One of few seaside amusement parks left on the US West Coast

w: Established in 1953, this 4,623-acre park protects old-growth coast redwood groves and riparian forest along the San Lorenzo River, between Santa Cruz and Scotts Valley near Felton. A separate, non-contiguous extension covers the Fall Creek area to the north.
s: Old-growth redwood grove along the San Lorenzo River
_facts: Preserves an old-growth coast redwood grove
Non-contiguous Fall Creek extension north of Felton

w: Founded in 1791 by Father Fermin Francisco de Lasuen, successor to Junipero Serra, it flooded on the San Lorenzo floodplain and was rebuilt on Mission Hill. Most was later razed for Holy Cross Church in 1889; a 1930s replica chapel remains beside the sole surviving 1822-24 adobe, oldest building in Santa Cruz County.
s: 1791 mission replica beside its one surviving adobe
_facts: Founded August 28, 1791 by Fermin Francisco de Lasuen
Original site flooded, relocated to Mission Hill
Most of the second mission razed in 1889 for Holy Cross Church
Surviving 1822-24 adobe is the oldest structure in Santa Cruz County

w: Built in 2001 in the Santa Cruz Small Craft Harbor, this lighthouse is known locally as Walton Lighthouse, after Charles Walton, who gave 60,000 dollars toward its construction in memory of his brother Derek, a merchant seaman. It is distinct from the older Santa Cruz Light, 1.5 miles west above Steamer Lane.
s: Harbor lighthouse named for a merchant seaman's memory
_facts: Located in the Santa Cruz Small Craft Harbor
Known as Walton Lighthouse after donor Charles Walton
Distinct from the older Santa Cruz Light near Steamer Lane

w: Built in 1888-89 for Alfred Joseph Hinds and his wife Sarah, this Victorian house is the largest surviving Stick-Eastlake style building in Santa Cruz County. Listed on the National Register of Historic Places since 1983 as the A. J. Hinds House, it now operates as a historic inn with rooms rented to guests.
s: Largest surviving Stick-Eastlake house in the county
